notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2022, as the township reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2022 is the latest available.
Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included. Residents also pay Richland County.
A township serves the parts of it outside cities, and in most cases also the villages inside it.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: Ohio local candidates file campaign finance reports with their county board of elections, not with the state.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Real-time crime center
redFlags.detail: The Mansfield Division of Police received a $120,000 state grant to establish a real time crime center.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS015043, citing State of Ohio

redFlags.label: Gunshot detection (ShotSpotter)
redFlags.detail: The Mansfield Police Department received a $272,000 state grant to increase the square mileage covered by gunshot detection technology in 2024. The agency acquired ShotSpotter gunshot detection technology in 2020.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS008053, citing ShotSpotter

redFlags.label: License-plate readers
redFlags.detail: As of April 2024, the Mansfield Police Department operates 29 Flock Safety automated license plate readers. The agency stores ALPR data for 30 days.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS001562, citing Flock Safety

redFlags.label: Police drones
redFlags.detail: The Mansfield Police Department purchased three DJI drones for $20,000 in 2018.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS002862, citing Mansfield Police Department
